title: M-x utilz offers 13 utilities; 4 error, 3 print usage, 1 mutates on selection
body:
## Tags

emacs-bridge, integration, declared-vs-actual, latent

## Summary

**Of the 13 utilities `M-x utilz` offers, 4 error on invocation, 3 return a usage dump, and 1 mutates the filesystem on selection.** Only `cleanz`, `expz` and `pdf2md` are cleanly coherent; `syncz` is coherent and dangerous.

The `integration:` blocks describe what each utility's I/O *shape* is, but not what its command line actually needs. Every one of the 13 declares `flags: []`, so a utility that takes a verb receives none and refuses.

Raised by hv on 2026-09-03 from the live menu: *"not all of those make sense inside an Emacs session, and some that might, are not there."*

## Reproduction

Run exactly what `utilz--build-cmdline` constructs for each declared input kind:

| utility  | bridge invokes            | result                                                        |
| -------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cryptz` | `utilz cryptz <file>`     | **rc=1** `Unknown command: <file>` -- needs `encrypt`/`decrypt` |
| `gitz`   | `utilz gitz <dir>`        | **rc=1** `Unknown command: <dir>` -- needs `status-all`        |
| `retry`  | `utilz retry`             | **rc=1** `No command provided` -- nothing to retry             |
| `mdagg`  | `<region> \| utilz mdagg` | **rc=1** `No input specified` -- mdagg does not read stdin     |
| `macoz`  | `utilz macoz`             | rc=0, prints its own usage; bridge echoes it as a "message"   |
| `clipz`  | `utilz clipz`             | rc=0, prints its own usage; same                               |
| `todo`   | `utilz todo`              | rc=0, empty view unless cwd happens to hold a `todo.md`       |
| `xtrct`  | `<region> \| utilz xtrct` | rc=1 without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; legitimate, fails loudly    |
| `lnrel`  | `utilz lnrel <dir>`       | **rc=0 AND CREATES A SYMLINK** in the prompted directory      |

`lnrel` is the sharp one: selecting it from a completing-read menu mutates the filesystem, with no confirmation, and reports success. `syncz` (`path -> buffer`) has the same shape and was not run for that reason -- it would fire a directory sync.

## Root Cause

**The blocks were filled in as a matrix rather than derived per utility.** CHANGELOG 2.2.0 records it: *"All 12 current utilities now carry an `integration:` block."* Twelve blocks were authored in one pass from each utility's I/O shape, which is the half the TSV contract is about, and nothing checked that the resulting command line was one the utility would accept.

**The mechanism to fix it already exists and is unused.** `integration.flags` reaches the TSV as field 5, and `utilz--build-cmdline` splits it on `,` and inserts it before the path argument. Every utility declares `flags: []`. Verified that populating it works:

- `utilz gitz status-all .` -> rc=0
- `utilz prez build deck.md` -> `prez: wrote deck.html`, 22710 bytes

So `gitz` needs `flags: [status-all]` and the verb-taking utilities need their verb. That is a declaration fix, not a code fix.

**Nothing can catch this class today.** `utilz emacs doctor` checks that a block's *values* are valid (issue 0006 made an absent block a non-failure and an invalid value a real one), but a block can be entirely valid and still describe a command line the utility refuses. No test invokes what the bridge would build.

## Impact

Medium. It does not affect any utility's CLI behaviour and never has -- the whole defect lives at the bridge boundary. But the menu is the only surface most Emacs use goes through, and a user's first experience of eight of thirteen entries is an error buffer, a usage dump, or an unexpected symlink.

The `lnrel` case is the one worth separating: **a menu entry that mutates the filesystem on selection is a different severity from one that errors.** An error is self-correcting; a symlink created in a directory the user merely pointed at is not.

## Resolution

**hv ruled on 2026-09-03: prune rather than repair.** In hv's words: *"I don't need them all there, tbh. I just need the ones that make sense to be there. cleanz is the main one that I use and I use that all the time."*

The menu goes from **13 entries to 5**:

| utility  | action                                            | why                                                                 |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cleanz` | keep, unchanged (`stdin -> replace`)              | the motivating case and hv's daily use                              |
| `expz`   | keep, unchanged (`path -> buffer`)                | works; point at a receipts directory, CSV in a buffer               |
| `pdf2md` | keep, unchanged (`file -> buffer`)                | works; converts the file you are visiting                           |
| `mdagg`  | keep, INPUT KIND CORRECTED `stdin` -> `path`      | it does not read stdin; declared shape was wrong, not merely odd    |
| `prez`   | **added** (`file -> message`, `flags: [build]`)   | you are editing a deck in a markdown buffer and one command builds it |
| `clipz`  | block removed                                     | Emacs has its own clipboard and kill ring; printed its usage        |
| `macoz`  | block removed                                     | printed its usage; not buffer work                                  |
| `cryptz` | block removed                                     | needs an `encrypt`/`decrypt` verb that does not collapse to one entry |
| `retry`  | block removed                                     | `input: none` leaves it nothing to retry                            |
| `gitz`   | block removed                                     | needed `status-all`, and Emacs has magit                            |
| `xtrct`  | block removed                                     | needs an API key AND a `--schema` the menu cannot supply            |
| `todo`   | block removed                                     | shows whatever `todo.md` is in cwd; context-dependent               |
| `lnrel`  | **block removed on safety grounds**               | created a symlink on selection, rc=0, no confirmation               |
| `syncz`  | **block removed on safety grounds**               | same shape: a directory sync one keystroke from a fuzzy menu        |

`stampz` is deliberately NOT added: `path -> message` is the right shape but it needs a recipient, which only reaches it through the `C-u` extra-flags prompt. Its absence is now a decision rather than a scaffolding default.

**A test now invokes what the bridge would build**, per declaring utility, and asserts a non-error exit. That is the check whose absence let a valid-looking block describe an impossible command line: `utilz emacs doctor` validates a block's VALUES, and every one of these blocks was valid.

## Proposed Fix (as diagnosed, before hv's ruling)

Three parts, and the first is hv's ruling rather than a code change.

1. **Decide which utilities belong in an editor menu at all.** Absence is already a legitimate state (issue 0006's fix made an unbound utility a non-failure), so the honest move for `clipz` (Emacs has its own clipboard and kill ring), `macoz`, `retry` and `lnrel` is likely to drop the block rather than repair it. `syncz` is a judgement call: coherent, useful, and a filesystem mutation one keystroke from a fuzzy-match menu.
2. **Populate `flags:` for the ones that stay** and take a verb -- `gitz: [status-all]`, `cryptz: [encrypt]` (or drop it; the encrypt/decrypt split does not survive a single menu entry), `mdagg`'s input kind is wrong and should be `path` or `file` rather than `stdin`.
3. **Add `prez`, which is the strongest missing fit.** `input: file`, `output: message`, `flags: [build]`: you are editing a deck in a markdown buffer and one command builds it. Verified working. `stampz` is marginal -- `path -> message` is right, but it needs a recipient, which only reaches it through the `C-u` extra-flags prompt.
4. **Add a test that invokes what the bridge would build**, per declaring utility, and asserts a non-error exit or a named skip. That is the check whose absence let a valid-looking block describe an impossible command line.

## Related

- ST0007 -- the thread that authored the twelve blocks as a matrix
- 0006 -- made an absent `integration:` block a non-failure, which is what makes "drop the block" a legitimate fix here
- ST0011 -- `stampz` ships with no block; that was a default, not a decision, and this issue is where the decision belongs

## Correction, 2026-09-03 -- `todo` restored

**`todo` was removed in the pass above and the reason given was wrong.** hv caught it: *"todo: why did we drop that? That should work in emacs. If I have a todo.md file in the buffer, then I should be able to apply 'utilz todo...' commands to it, right?"*

The measurement was right and the conclusion did not follow. `utilz todo` with `input: none` runs in whatever directory Emacs happens to be in and ignores the buffer entirely -- so it was useless. But that is a **broken declaration, not a utility that does not belong in an editor**, and it is the identical defect to `mdagg`'s `input: stdin`. `mdagg` was corrected and `todo` was dropped. Same evidence, two conclusions, and nothing in the reasoning distinguished them.

Restored as `input: file`, `output: buffer`, `flags: [--file]`, which builds `utilz todo --file <buffer's file>` -- visiting a `todo.md` and picking it shows that file's DOING/TODO/DONE view.

**Verified read-only.** `input: file` offers whatever buffer you are in, so a view that stamped an arbitrary file would be a bad surprise. Hashed before and after on both a real `todo.md` and an unrelated markdown file; neither was touched.

**The `C-u` extra-flags path does not work here and fails loudly, which is the better of the two behaviours available.** The bridge inserts extra flags BETWEEN the declared flags and the path, so `C-u ... done 2` builds `utilz todo --file "done 2" <path>` and exits 1. The alternative -- `flags: []`, letting the path land last -- builds `utilz todo done 2 <path>`, which exits 0 having modified `./todo.md` instead of the file on screen. **A loud refusal beats a silent write to the wrong file**, so the ordering limitation is left in place rather than worked around.

Menu is six, not five.
